findings.claim: A concurrent publication can expose a local command ledger after its migration commits and before the publication event trigger is installed by migration 2026090605.
findings.evidence: The runner explicitly states that server migrations commit separately, performs only a preflight at line 114, and installs aso_local_command_publication_guard in the fifth migration; the postflight detects an unsafe publication only after the exposure window.
findings.suggested_fix: Install the publication guard before any ledger-creating migration can commit, or hold a database-level exclusion mechanism honored by publication DDL across the entire separately committed migration sequence.

findings.claim: The publication guard can be bypassed by renaming a command-ledger table before explicitly publishing it.
findings.evidence: The event trigger ran only for CREATE PUBLICATION and ALTER PUBLICATION, while its predicate identified protected relations solely by mutable table names. ALTER TABLE RENAME was not inspected.
findings.suggested_fix: Track protected relations by durable identity or immutable metadata and test rename then publish.

findings.claim: An uncertain HTTP gateway failure discards the command ID required to reconcile a reassessment that may already have committed.
findings.evidence: The catch block retained commandId only for non-ApiError failures; every ApiError outside capability and precondition cases cleared lastCommandId. Gateway 502, 503, 504, or timeout responses can arrive after commit. use-surgeon-gate.ts used the same classification.
findings.suggested_fix: Retain the scoped command ID for transport-uncertain HTTP statuses and network exceptions; clear it only when the response conclusively proves no commit.

findings.claim: Production composition leaves an existing mounted evidence-count route permanently unavailable.
findings.evidence: PgGateRepository counts always returns DomainError::Storage while the actorless route remained mounted.
findings.suggested_fix: Implement a verified PostgreSQL read before mounting, or unmount the endpoint until its verified-context contract exists.
